note: He is the purest good-to-great case in the batch and simultaneously fails the criterion that is supposed to describe the same thing. Health is not his neglected area — he is a yoga teacher with a four-year movement-school background, a serious dancer, a carb cycler and a former calisthenics specialist. The stated ICP assumes the buyer is a successful person whose body has been let slide; this buyer's body is the most cultivated thing about him, and what he wants is a level above his own ceiling. He owns a therapy practice so he clears 'successful' on occupation, but he misses on income in the practical sense the criterion is testing: $5-6k a month revenue, $1-2k monthly surplus after multiple rents, a Payva financing application declined on the call and a hard $2,000 ceiling on what his card would carry today. He closed anyway, on three interest-free instalments. That is the same pattern already logged in data/icp.json against the Francisco Vega assessment — income screening is filtering on a criterion the payment plan is already solving, and here it would have excluded a textbook-fit optimizer.
